feat(workflows): add advisory Dependabot PR reviewer agentic workflow (#498)

## Description

Adds an advisory-only agentic review workflow that runs on every
Dependabot pull request in this repository. The workflow enriches each
dependency bump with GHSA, OSV, and NVD advisory intel plus ecosystem
release notes, classifies risk against this repo's dependency surfaces,
and posts exactly one review with an **APPROVE** or **COMMENT** verdict.
It never emits `REQUEST_CHANGES` and never blocks a merge.

The feature lands as three coordinated artifacts under `.github/`: the
*gh-aw* source workflow at
**`.github/workflows/aw-dependabot-pr-review.md`**, the reviewer persona
at **`.github/agents/dependabot-pr-reviewer.agent.md`**, and the
compiled **`.github/workflows/aw-dependabot-pr-review.lock.yml`**
emitted by `gh aw compile` (v0.68.7). Supporting changes register the
new gh-aw config variables with *actionlint*, extend the cspell
allowlist, document the flow in the contributor guide, and fix an
unrelated filename mismatch that was blocking the *lerobot-eval* image
build.

Closes #496

Additional components touched by this PR:

- **`.github/agents/`** — new dispatcher and reviewer agent personas.

The lock file is generated by `gh aw compile` (v0.68.7) from the source

sources (GHSA / OSV / NVD), surface-specific risk flags (Isaac Sim

Actions tags), and the maintainer-authority disclaimer.

unblocking the SIL *lerobot* evaluation image build.

format](instructions/commit-message.instructions.md)

- [x] Documentation impact assessed above
- [ ] No new linting warnings introduced

### Changes at a Glance

#### Advisory reviewer workflow

The new *gh-aw* workflow triggers on `pull_request` (opened,
synchronize, reopened) filtered by dependency manifests —
*package.json*, *pnpm-lock.yaml*, *pyproject.toml*, *uv.lock*,
*requirements*.txt*, *go.mod*, *go.sum*, *\*.tf*, *\*.tfvars*, and
*Dockerfile\**, with an explicit `!.github/workflows/**` exclusion — and
gates on `bots: ["dependabot[bot]"]`. Permissions are least-privilege
(`contents: read`, `pull-requests: read`) and the network allowlist
enumerates ecosystems (`github`, `python`, `node`, `go`, `terraform`,
`containers`) plus **api.osv.dev** and **services.nvd.nist.gov**.
`pre-agent-steps` install *jq*, *Terraform 1.9.8* via SHA-pinned
`hashicorp/setup-terraform`, and *TFLint* via SHA-pinned
`terraform-linters/setup-tflint`.

The `safe-outputs` block caps output at five inline review comments, one
review submission, two PR comments, and one `noop` — preventing runaway
commentary even on grouped PRs.

#### Reviewer persona

The persona in **`.github/agents/dependabot-pr-reviewer.agent.md`**
defines the review contract: parse the Dependabot *Updates* table
row-by-row, extract `GHSA-*` and `CVE-*` identifiers, walk the
enrichment chain (*GitHub Advisory API* → *OSV.dev* → *NVD*), pull
release notes from the ecosystem registry (*PyPI*, *npm*, *Go proxy*,
*Terraform registry*, *Docker Hub*), and apply an ecosystem surface
rubric that calls out this repo's specific sensitivities — most notably
the Isaac Sim *numpy* pin `>=1.26.0,<2.0.0` under `training/rl/`,
`azurerm` major bumps across `infrastructure/terraform/**`,
CUDA-adjacent base images, and action-tag (non-SHA) replacements.
High-risk triggers prepend a `⚠️ Maintainer review recommended` banner
and force the verdict to **COMMENT**. `REQUEST_CHANGES` is forbidden in
every condition, as are fabricated CVE/GHSA IDs and opinions on merge
timing.

#### Compiled lock file

The 1448-line **`.github/workflows/aw-dependabot-pr-review.lock.yml`**
is auto-generated by *gh-aw v0.68.7* and implements a six-job pipeline:
`pre_activation` → `activation` → `agent` + `detection` + `safe_outputs`
→ `conclusion`. Every third-party action is SHA-pinned; the MCP gateway
pins to digest `v0.2.22`; the GitHub MCP server runs in read-only mode;
and the *AWF* firewall (v0.25.23) enforces the domain allowlist. The
`detection` job re-runs Copilot over agent outputs as a second-pass
threat review after clearing MCP configs. Treat the lock file as
generated output — regenerate via `gh aw compile` rather than
hand-editing.

#### Dispatcher agent and tooling config

Added **`.github/agents/agentic-workflows.agent.md`** as a dispatcher
persona that routes *gh-aw* work (create, update, debug, upgrade,
report, shared components, Dependabot fix, test-coverage) to the
appropriate specialized prompts. Registered the two new *gh-aw* config
variables `gh_aw_model_agent_copilot` and
`gh_aw_model_detection_copilot` in **`.github/actionlint.yaml`** so
actionlint accepts the compiled workflow, and added `cves` and `vulns`
to **`.cspell/industry-acronyms.txt`** for the new agent prose.

#### Contributor documentation

Revised the *Dependabot PR flow* sentence in
**`docs/contributing/component-updates.md`** to insert the advisory
reviewer between CI and maintainer review, and added a new **Advisory
Reviewer Agent** subsection summarizing enrichment sources,
surface-specific risk flags, inline-comment caps, the
drafts-and-workflows skip rule, and the advisory posture.

#### Dockerfile filename fix

Corrected the `COPY` and `uv pip install` filename references in
**`evaluation/sil/docker/Dockerfile.lerobot-eval`** from the
non-existent `requirements-lerobot-infer.txt` to the real
`requirements-lerobot-eval.txt`, unblocking the SIL *lerobot* evaluation
image build.

### Related Issues

Closes #496

### Follow-up

- Configure the **`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`** repository (or org) secret
before merge — the lock file validates this secret at job start and will
fail the run if it is missing.
- The `vars.GH_AW_MODEL_AGENT_COPILOT` /
`vars.GH_AW_MODEL_DETECTION_COPILOT` Actions variables are **optional**
(they fall back to the engine default model); set them only to pin a
specific Copilot model. > NOTE the **`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`** has been
set, the optional ones have not.

- Dependabot coverage gaps called out in
*docs/contributing/component-updates.md* persist: *Helm charts*,
*container images*, and *infrastructure/terraform/vpn/* +
*infrastructure/terraform/automation/* still need manual updates.
- The persona references *training/il/lerobot/pyproject.toml* as an
uncovered-manifest example; a follow-up PR could add it to
**.github/dependabot.yml**.

---------

+---
+name: AW Dependabot PR Review
+description: Advisory agentic review of Dependabot dependency update PRs for physical-ai-toolchain

+  python:

+    action-version: 4a3601121dd01d1626a1e23e37211e3254c1c06c # v6.4.0
+pre-agent-steps:
+  - name: Install jq for Dependabot body and JSON intel parsing
+    shell: bash
+    run: |
+      set -euo pipefail
+      if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        sudo apt-get update

+  - name: Set up Terraform
+    uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@5e8dbf3c6d9deaf4193ca7a8fb23f2ac83bb6c85 # v4.0.0

+---
+
+# Dependabot PR Review
+
+Advisory-only review of Dependabot-authored pull requests in microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain. The agent classifies risk, enriches findings with GHSA/OSV/NVD intel and release notes, and posts a single review plus targeted inline comments. It never blocks merges.
+
+## Posture
+
+* **Advisory only.** Submit exactly one review with `event: APPROVE` or `event: COMMENT`. `REQUEST_CHANGES` is forbidden.
+* **High-risk findings** surface as a `⚠️ Maintainer review recommended` banner in the review body; the verdict still stays on the `APPROVE` / `COMMENT` allowlist.
+* **Scope.** Only Dependabot pull requests that touch declared dependency manifests (npm, uv/pip, Go modules, Terraform, Docker). All other diffs are out of scope.
+
+## Gating
+
+Skip the review and emit a `noop` when any of the following hold:
+
+* Pull request author is not `dependabot[bot]`.
+* Pull request is a draft (`github.event.pull_request.draft == true`).
+* Diff touches `.github/workflows/**` — workflow changes are reviewed by `dependency-review`, `workflow-permissions-scan`, and `sha-staleness-check` instead.
+* Diff contains no recognized dependency manifest change.
+
+## Agent Persona
+
+The full reviewer persona, risk rubric, ecosystem-specific checks, and enrichment playbook are defined in the imported agent file [`.github/agents/dependabot-pr-reviewer.agent.md`](../agents/dependabot-pr-reviewer.agent.md). Follow it verbatim.
+
+## Step-by-Step
+
+1. **Parse.** Read the pull request title, body, and file diff. Extract package name, ecosystem, old/new versions, `GHSA-[0-9a-z]{4}-[0-9a-z]{4}-[0-9a-z]{4}` and `CVE-\d{4}-\d{4,7}` identifiers from the Dependabot body.
+2. **Enrich.** Query GHSA (preferred), fall back to OSV (`api.osv.dev`) and NVD (`services.nvd.nist.gov`) for severity, affected ranges, and fixed versions. Fetch release notes or changelog via the relevant package registry (npm, PyPI, Go module proxy, Terraform registry).
+3. **Classify.** Apply the persona's per-surface rubric. Flag ABI-sensitive pins (for example `numpy >=1.26.0,<2.0.0` in Isaac Sim training), pre-1.0 bumps, major version jumps, and missing upstream advisories.
+4. **Review.** Post up to five inline `create-pull-request-review-comment` entries for specific risks, up to two `add-comment` status updates on the triggering PR, and exactly one `submit-pull-request-review` with `APPROVE` or `COMMENT`. When nothing actionable is found, emit `noop`.
+
+Keep comments factual and concise. Cite the advisory identifier, affected versions, and the Dependabot PR URL.

feat(agents): add automated validation for high-risk Dependabot bumps (#574)

Enhanced the Dependabot PR reviewer agentic workflow to execute lint and
test suites when a high-risk dependency bump is detected (e.g.,
`pyarrow` major version crossing an ABI boundary). Previously, the agent
could only *advise* maintainers to run checks manually — it now executes
them directly and reports concrete pass/fail results in the review body.

> Motivated by PR #565 where a `pyarrow 23.0.1 → 24.0.0` bump was
flagged as high-risk but required manual `ruff check` + `pytest` to
confirm compatibility. The workflow had all runtimes pre-configured and
bash tool access — it should have done this itself.

## Description

### Agent Validation Logic

Added a **Validation Execution** section to the
*dependabot-pr-reviewer.agent.md* with structured rules for when and how
to run checks:

- Per-surface command table mapping trigger conditions to exact
validation commands across 6 surfaces (python-runtime
dataviewer/evaluation/training, dataviewer-frontend,
terraform-providers, gomod)
- **Reporting format** requiring a `### Validation Results` block with
commands executed, pass/fail counts, and a clear ✅/⚠️ status line
- **Verdict adjustment** rules allowing upgrade from `COMMENT` →
`APPROVE` when all checks pass, keeping `COMMENT` when they fail or are
skipped
- Execution rules capping validation at 5 minutes and skipping low-risk
patches entirely

- Fixed invalid `pre-agent-steps:` field → `steps:` to match the current
gh-aw schema (resolved a compilation error, this was likely due to a

authored. Pinned back to latest Release v0.68.3 to ensure stability.)

feat(workflows): trigger AW Dependabot PR reviewer after PR Validation (#580)

## Description

Rewired the AW Dependabot PR Review workflow to fire *after* the `PR
Validation` orchestrator finishes instead of racing it on `pull_request`
events, replaced the agent persona's unreachable in-sandbox validation

and `go` inside the AWF firewall sandbox, but those binaries live on the
host runner and are never mounted into the container. The agent reported

Additional note:

the current AWF capabilities. The long-term solution may involve

## Changes

### Trigger migration: `pull_request` → `workflow_run`

The workflow previously fired on `pull_request` events with path filters
for dependency manifests. This meant the agent ran in parallel with CI
and could finalize its verdict before slow check suites completed —
producing approvals that later contradicted red merge gates.

- Switched the trigger to `workflow_run` after the **`PR Validation`**
orchestrator completes, so the agent has final per-job pass/fail
conclusions before reasoning about the PR.
- Added a **`resolve-pr`** step using `actions/github-script@v9` that
extracts the Dependabot PR context from the `workflow_run` payload. The
step implements two-tier PR resolution (direct from
`workflow_run.pull_requests` → search API fallback for forks) and
exports `PR_VALIDATION_CONCLUSION`, `PR_NUMBER`, `PR_HEAD_SHA`, and
other context as environment variables.
- Removed `bots:`, `reaction:`, and `status-comment:` frontmatter keys
(not applicable under `workflow_run` context).
- Simplified concurrency from per-PR grouping to per-workflow singleton
— consistent with `workflow_run` semantics where `pull_request.number`
is not in the event payload.
- Updated activation and pre-activation `if:` conditions to validate
`workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'` with fork guards via
`repository.id` and `!(repository.fork)`.
- Added `# zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]` annotations at the
trigger and activation condition with justification that the trigger is
secured with role and fork validation.

### Persona rewrite: Validation Execution → Validation Signal

The old "Validation Execution" section instructed the agent to run `uv
sync`, `pytest`, `ruff check`, `npm ci`, `terraform validate`, and `go
vet` inside the AWF firewall sandbox. Those binaries are installed on
the host runner but never mounted into the sandbox container — every
invocation failed, producing the misleading `⚠️ Validation skipped`
banner observed in PR #577.

- Replaced the entire section with **Validation Signal** anchored on
three sources: deterministic CI check-run conclusions, static manifest
reasoning, and advisory enrichment.
- Added a **Surface to Check Run Map** table mapping 10 surfaces
(dataviewer-frontend, python-runtime variants, terraform, gomod, docker,
github-actions) to their authoritative CI check run names.
- Added **Static Impact Reasoning** with five manifest-level checks the
sandbox *can* do safely: Isaac Sim ABI guard (`numpy>=1.26.0,<2.0.0`),
torch/tensordict/onnxruntime-gpu flagging, dataviewer peer-dep conflict
detection via `npm view`, terraform provider changelog scraping via
`web-fetch`, and go module direct major quoting.
- Rewrote **Verdict Adjustment** to key off `PR_VALIDATION_CONCLUSION` —
green CI with clean static reasoning may upgrade to `APPROVE`; red CI
forces `COMMENT` with failing check-run names and URLs. The Isaac Sim
ABI guard is "sticky": a `numpy` 2.x bump keeps the verdict at `COMMENT`
regardless of CI.
- Added a `## Trigger Posture` section to the workflow prompt
documenting the `workflow_run` model, exported env vars, and sandbox
constraints.
- Expanded **Step-by-Step** from 4 to 6 steps — added context resolution
and CI signal reading as steps 1–2. Explicit instruction to never skip
enrichment on red CI so maintainers can triage grouped PRs.

### Bash allow-list cleanup

- Removed **11 dead entries** from the `tools.bash:` allow-list that
invoked `uv`, `pytest`, `npm ci`, `terraform`, and `go` — all
unreachable inside the AWF firewall container.
- Added **2 targeted entries**: `cat training/rl/requirements.txt` and
`cat training/rl/scripts/train.sh` to support the Isaac Sim ABI guard
static check.

### Permissions and lifecycle cleanup

- Dropped `discussions: write`, `issues: write`, and `pull-requests:
write` from the activation job (no longer needed without the
reaction/comment steps).
- Added `actions: read` to both activation and copilot jobs (required
for check-run queries).
- Removed the eyes-reaction, body-computation, workflow-run-comment, and
conclusion-notification steps — the `workflow_run` trigger has no direct
PR event to react to.

- The lock file (`.github/workflows/aw-dependabot-pr-review.lock.yml`)
was recompiled via `gh aw compile`, which changes metadata hashes and
heredoc delimiters throughout — these are mechanical changes, not
hand-edits.
- The review will now appear 5–15 minutes later than the old
`pull_request` trigger (after CI completes), but the trade-off is
accurate CI signal in every review.
- The agent retains its advisory-only posture (`APPROVE` or `COMMENT`,
never `REQUEST_CHANGES`) and its safe-output caps (5 inline comments, 1
review, 2 add-comments).

the persona's docker surface row currently never fires because no
Dockerfile entries are configured.

host directories into the sandbox, which would re-enable in-agent
validation as a complementary signal.

The **AW Dependabot PR Review** workflow stopped firing for every
Dependabot PR after PR #580 introduced the `pull_request` →
`workflow_run` trigger migration. The `branches:` filter was set to

## Description

The *AW Dependabot PR Review* agentic workflow was firing on Dependabot
PRs but its review output was being silently dropped — every
`create_pull_request_review_comment` and `submit_pull_request_review`
message was skipped by the `safe_outputs` job with *"Not in pull request

## Description

The `aw-dependabot-pr-review` agentic workflow used to fire on
`pull_request_target`, which meant the resolver step captured a snapshot
of `PR Validation` while it was still `pending` or `in_progress:*`, and
the advisory review was posted before the orchestrator ever finished. PR
#608 was the canonical example: the review correctly applied the Isaac
Sim *numpy 2.x* ABI guard, but its CI banner quoted a stale
`in_progress:in_progress` conclusion.

This PR migrates the workflow to `workflow_run` keyed on `PR Validation`
*completed*, reads the orchestrator's terminal conclusion straight from
`context.payload.workflow_run.conclusion`, and pre-resolves failing
per-surface check-runs once in the resolver step. The persona rubric is
rewritten to consume those env vars and to map every terminal conclusion
explicitly - `pending` and `in_progress:*` branches are gone because
they are now unreachable.

Related to #579.

["PR Validation"]`**, `types: [completed]`, `branches:
["dependabot/**"]`. The `branches:` filter on `workflow_run` matches the
*triggering run's `head_branch`* (not the base), so `dependabot/**` is
the only value that fires for Dependabot PRs — using `main` here was the
[#583](https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/issues/583)
regression fixed in
[#584](https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/pull/584). The
workflow-level `if:` filters on `workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'`,
`workflow_run.actor.login == 'dependabot[bot]'`, and a whitelist of
seven terminal conclusions.

write]` at the top level — gh-aw's `pre_activation` guard checks the
triggering actor against `on.bots` / `on.roles` independently of the
workflow `if:`, so dropping these would resurrect the
[#585](https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/issues/585) /
[#586](https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/pull/586)
`User permission 'none'` activation block.
- Added `checks: read` to `permissions:` for server-side check-run
enumeration; existing `contents`, `pull-requests`, and `actions` scopes
are unchanged.
- Rewrote the *resolve-pr* step. It reads
`context.payload.workflow_run`, prefers `workflow_run.pull_requests[0]`,
and falls back to `search.issuesAndPullRequests` keyed on `head_sha` for
the fork case. Both paths re-hydrate via `pulls.get` so `body` and
`draft` are reliable.
- Dropped the previous `listWorkflowRunsForRepo` lookup.
**`PR_VALIDATION_CONCLUSION`** now reads directly from `run.conclusion`,
which under `types: [completed]` is always one of `success`, `failure`,
`cancelled`, `timed_out`, `neutral`, `skipped`, or `action_required`.
- Added two new env vars exported by the resolver:
- **`PR_VALIDATION_FAILING_CHECKS`** — JSON array of `{name, html_url,
conclusion}` from `checks.listForRef(ref=pr.head.sha)` filtered to
completed non-success/non-neutral/non-skipped runs.
- **`PR_BODY`** — PR body hydrated server-side so the agent does not
depend on the integrity-filtered MCP read of the PR.
- New skip reasons in `PR_DEPENDABOT_SKIP_REASON`: `not-a-pr-run` and
`pr-resolution-failed`, alongside the existing `not-dependabot` /
`draft`.
- Retargeted `safe-outputs`:
  - `submit-pull-request-review.target` → `${{ env.PR_NUMBER }}`
- `add-comment.target` → `${{ env.PR_NUMBER }}` (was `triggering`, which
is undefined under `workflow_run`)
  - `create-pull-request-review-comment.target` → `"*"`

### Persona verdict rubric

> The agent now reasons over a *final* CI signal, so the rubric
collapses to a clean terminal-conclusion map.

- Rewrote the *Validation Signal* section in
`.github/agents/dependabot-pr-reviewer.agent.md`. The persona is told
the workflow runs after `PR Validation` reaches a terminal conclusion,
and is explicitly forbidden from calling `checks.listForRef` or
`commits/{sha}/check-runs` — it reads `PR_VALIDATION_FAILING_CHECKS`
from the environment instead.
- Reframed the *Surface to Check Run Map* as an informational lookup for
mapping a failing check name back to its dependency surface. The persona
no longer walks it via the API.
- Rewrote the *Verdict Adjustment* block as an explicit
terminal-conclusion map:

'pr-resolution-failed'` → `COMMENT` with a `> [!CAUTION]` banner:
*Deterministic CI signal unavailable (`{conclusion}`); review is
advisory only.*

still keeps the verdict at `COMMENT` and forces the `⚠️ Maintainer
review recommended` banner regardless of CI conclusion.

model, the gh-aw compiler's auto-injected fork-PR exclusion and

## Description

The **AW Dependabot PR Review** agentic workflow silently skipped on
every run and never posted a review. It was triggered by `workflow_run`
after *PR Validation* completed on a `dependabot/**` branch, so the
triggering actor was `dependabot[bot]` (permission `none`). gh-aw's

and skipped all downstream jobs without failing — a green run that
produced no advisory.

`/aw-dependabot-review` **slash command**. A maintainer comments
`/aw-dependabot-review` on a Dependabot PR, and gh-aw's role gate now
evaluates the *commenter* (a maintainer with `write`+) rather than
`dependabot[bot]`, so activation passes and the review runs. The
slash-command posture also sidesteps the gh-aw compiler bug that blocked
a `bots:`/`roles:` allowlist alongside `workflow_run`.

The change touches the workflow source
(`.github/workflows/aw-dependabot-pr-review.md`), its recompiled lock
file, the reviewer persona
(`.github/agents/dependabot-pr-reviewer.agent.md`), and the contributor
docs (`docs/contributing/component-updates.md`).

fix(agents): make Dependabot reviewer COMMENT-only (#976)

## Description

The *AW Dependabot PR Review* agentic workflow failed in its
`safe_outputs` job whenever the agent decided a PR looked safe. It
emitted a `submit-pull-request-review` with `event: APPROVE`, and GitHub
rejected it with *"GitHub Actions is not permitted to approve pull
requests."* This is a hard platform restriction on the
**`GITHUB_TOKEN`** identity, not a missing permission scope.

event was removed everywhere it appeared in the agent persona and the
workflow spec, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` stays forbidden so the agent never
gates a merge. The "safe to merge" signal is preserved as an **advisory
recommendation** rendered in the review body, decoupled from the GitHub
review event so a human reviewer still provides the actual approval. The
compiled *lock* file was regenerated from the edited source.

feat(ci): Standardize uv.lock as the single dependency resolution source of truth (#995)

This branch makes the committed `uv.lock` the single dependency
resolution source of truth for every Python subproject and stops
committing runtime-flat `requirements.txt` files. Each subproject now
keeps a `uv.lock` next to its `pyproject.toml`, and every runtime
install path — shell scripts, the SIL Dockerfile, and the OSMO/AzureML
workflow YAML — derives its requirement set at build or submit time with
`uv export --frozen --no-hashes --no-emit-project` rather than reading a
checked-in flat file. A new PowerShell linter and reusable workflow
enforce lock/manifest consistency in CI, and several security-driven
dependency pins are added through `override-dependencies` and
`constraint-dependencies` with the locks regenerated to match.

> The lock is the resolution contract. Removing the committed flat files
eliminates the drift surface between a hand-maintained
`requirements.txt` and the manifest it was compiled from, and lets
Dependabot regenerate locks natively while a read-only `uv lock --check`
gate blocks any PR whose lock drifts from its `pyproject.toml`.

## Description

### Runtime install paths now derive from the lock

The four runtime entrypoints and two OSMO workflows were rewritten to
export from the committed lock instead of reading a flat file:

- **evaluation/sil/evaluation.sh** and **evaluation/sil/infer.sh**
export from *training/il/lerobot/uv.lock* into a `mktemp` file and
install with `--project` context (full resolution, no `--no-deps`), with
the lockfile-presence guard and `trap` cleanup replacing the old
requirements checks.
- **training/rl/scripts/train.sh** and
**training/il/scripts/lerobot/azureml-train-entry.sh** pipe `uv export
--frozen ... | uv pip install --no-deps`.
- **training/il/workflows/osmo/lerobot-train.yaml** and
**evaluation/sil/workflows/osmo/lerobot-eval.yaml** replaced their
flat-file install steps with the same piped export, guarding on
`uv.lock` presence.
- **evaluation/sil/docker/Dockerfile.lerobot-eval** now copies
*pyproject.toml* and *uv.lock* and installs via `uv export --frozen | uv
pip install --system --no-deps`.
- **training/utils/replay-azureml.sh** adds `uv` to `require_tools` and
base64-encodes a submit-time export from *workflows/osmo/uv.lock*
instead of a committed *requirements-aml-mirror.txt*.

The committed flat files were removed:
*training/il/lerobot/requirements.txt* (651 lines),
*training/rl/requirements.txt* (519 lines),
*workflows/osmo/requirements-aml-mirror.txt* (511 lines), and
*evaluation/sil/docker/requirements-lerobot-eval.txt* (9 lines).

### New manifests and lock-target constraints

Two new manifests back previously flat-only runtimes:
*evaluation/sil/docker/pyproject.toml* (SIL LeRobot eval image) and
*workflows/osmo/pyproject.toml* (AzureML replay mirror), both with
`package = false` and a `[tool.uv] environments` marker constraining the
universal lock to the deployment target so `uv export` yields a
single-marker, runtime-flat set. The existing
*training/il/lerobot/pyproject.toml* and *training/rl/pyproject.toml*
gained the same `environments` constraint; the IL manifest also moved
`prerelease = "allow"` from `[tool.uv.pip]` to `[tool.uv]` so `uv lock`
honors it. The IL cuda-bindings comments were corrected from torch
2.11.0 to **torch 2.10.0**, matching lerobot's `torch<2.11` cap.

### Security-driven pins

`override-dependencies` and `constraint-dependencies` were extended with
security-patched versions, documented inline with GHSA identifiers:
**cryptography 48.0.1** (GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf) across the root, RL, IL,
SIL, OSMO, and viewer projects; **starlette 1.3.1** in the viewer
backend (SSRF, form DoS); and **diffusers 0.38.0** in the SIL image
(GHSA-98h9-4798-4q5v). The affected `uv.lock` files were regenerated,
including cryptography 46.0.7 → 48.0.1.

### CI enforcement

A new **scripts/linting/Invoke-UvLockConsistencyCheck.ps1** discovers
every directory containing a `uv.lock` (excluding *.venv/*, *external/*,
*node_modules/*, *.git/*, *.copilot-tracking/*, *docs/docusaurus/*),
runs `uv lock --check` per project, writes JSON results plus a step
summary, and exits non-zero on drift. It is covered by
*Invoke-UvLockConsistencyCheck.Tests.ps1* (Pester), exposed as
`lint:uvlock` in *package.json* (also appended to `lint:all`), and
wrapped by the reusable **.github/workflows/uv-lock-consistency.yml**.
The *pr-validation.yml* orchestrator runs it with `changed-files-only:
true`, and *main.yml* expanded its SBOM file list to cover the new
manifest/lock pairs and pinned `syft-version: v1.20.0`.

### Dependabot and documentation alignment

*.github/dependabot.yml* switched the evaluation entry to the `uv`
ecosystem, added an `av >= 16.0.0` ignore and a `torch` floor change,
and added a new `uv` entry for */workflows/osmo*. The Dependabot
reviewer agent and the `aw-dependabot-pr-review` workflow now reference
*training/rl/uv.lock* instead of *requirements.txt*. Documentation
across *copilot-instructions.md*, *CONTRIBUTING.md*,
*component-updates.md*, *pull-request-process.md*,
*lerobot-training.md*, *scripts-examples.md*, and
*infrastructure/setup/README.md* was updated to describe the
lock-as-source-of-truth flow, the `uv lock` regen command, and the new
CI gate.
